full_text_en:
Chen Long v. Shaanxi Boxin Sports Culture Communication Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over company dissolution

Ruling Summary

1. According to Article 16 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the shareholders' rights restricted due to the failure to perform or fully perform capital contribution obligations do not include the right to file a lawsuit for dissolution of the company.

2. The "serious difficulties" as provided in Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China include difficulties in external production and operation as well as difficulties in internal management.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2021) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 6453

Re-applicant (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Shaanxi Boxin Sports Culture Communication Co., Ltd. Domicile: West Side of the Third Floor of the Training Center Restaurant, Shaanxi Provincial Sports Training Center, No. 303 Zhangba Road, Gaoxin District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal representative: Ren Shuangcheng, executive director and general manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Hongbin, employee of the company.

Respondent (plaintiff at first instance, appellee at second instance): Chen Long, male, born on December 21, 1980, Han Chinese, residing in Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Bei, lawyer of Shaanxi Boshuo Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ding Jin'an, lawyer of Shaanxi Boshuo Law Firm.

Third party at first instance: Ren Shuangcheng, male, born on May 13, 1970, Han Chinese, residing in Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

The re-applicant Shaanxi Boxin Sports Culture Communication Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Boxin Company) filed an application with this Court for retrial of the case, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2021) Shaanxi Civil Final No. 206 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the dispute over company dissolution between the respondent Chen Long and the third party at first instance Ren Shuangcheng. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been concluded.

Boxin Company applied for retrial, alleging: (1) There are nine pieces of "new evidence": Evidence One, the company's articles of association. Evidence Two, a letter urging shareholder Chen Long to perform capital contribution obligations. Evidence Three, China Post EMS receipt. Evidence Four, Notarial Certificate (2019) Shaanxi Zheng Min Zi No. 004644. Evidence Five, notice of shareholders' meeting and resolutions. Evidence Six, Notarial Certificate (2019) Shaanxi Zheng Min Zi No. 005330. Evidence Seven, Notarial Certificate (2019) Shaanxi Zheng Min Zi No. 005331. Evidence Eight, "Urgent Notice on the Provision of Evidence Materials for Disciplinary Violations in Reports" (hereinafter referred to as the "Urgent Notice") issued by the Discipline Inspection Team of the Shaanxi Provincial Commission for Discipline Inspection in the Provincial Sports Bureau, and "Notice of Inquiry" No. Shaanxi Cultural Tourism Discipline Inspection and Supervision Inquiry Tong (2021) 5 issued by the Discipline Inspection and Supervision Team of the Shaanxi Provincial Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Provincial Supervisory Commission in the Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism. Evidence Nine, Criminal Ruling (2021) Shaanxi Criminal Final No. 132 of the Shaanxi High People's Court. The above evidence is used to prove the following objective facts: 1. Chen Long is a person participating in public administration as defined in the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China, and his equity participation and business activities are invalid because they are illegal. 2. Chen Long failed to perform his capital contribution obligations, violated the company's articles of association and relevant provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, and may not exercise shareholder rights. 3. The suspected illegal and criminal acts of Chen Long have been investigated by the disciplinary inspection commission and the public security authorities, including using violence and soft violence to force equity participation in the enterprise. (2) Based on the above facts, the second-instance judgment recognized Chen Long's shareholder qualification and ordered the dissolution of Boxin Company, violating the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws and regulations, allowing Chen Long to achieve the illegal purpose of profiting without capital through malicious litigation, which is extremely unfair to Boxin Company and Ren Shuangcheng, who actually contributed capital and independently operated the business. It should be corrected in accordance with the law to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the enterprise and the business environment. (3) The statutory conditions for Chen Long's application for company dissolution are not established, and the second-instance judgment applied the law improperly. Boxin Company has been operating and paying taxes legally since its establishment. Chen Long's reasons for requesting the dissolution of the company were "the company did not give him dividends" and no shareholders' meeting was held. In fact, Chen Long did not perform his capital contribution obligations at all. When the company urged him to contribute capital and participate in the shareholders' meeting, he refused. None of the dissolution reasons stated by Chen Long are supported by evidence. (4) The second-instance procedure was seriously illegal. This case was once remanded for retrial by the second-instance court on the ground of unclear facts. The first-instance court rendered the same judgment as before the retrial when the facts and evidence did not change, which suggests the possibility of bending the law for personal gain. The second-instance judgment failed to correct the errors of the first-instance judgment based on facts and law. In summary, Boxin Company requests a retrial of this case pursuant to Article 200, items 1, 2, and 6 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Chen Long submitted opinions, stating: (1) The facts found in the second-instance judgment are fully supported by evidence. Boxin Company's allegations in its application that Chen Long did not make capital contributions and that his identity did not comply with legal provisions lack factual basis. The fact that Chen Long is a shareholder of Boxin Company and has partially performed his capital contribution obligations has been confirmed by effective judgments of the people's court. Chen Long is the proper subject to sue for dissolution of the company. (2) The second-instance judgment applied the law correctly. On the one hand, Chen Long holds 49% of the shares in Boxin Company and has the right to request the people's court to dissolve the company in accordance with the law. On the other hand, since its establishment, Boxin Company has not held shareholders' meetings for a long time, and the two shareholders have been in long-term conflict. Boxin Company and Ren Shuangcheng once forged Chen Long's signature and issued false materials to change Chen Long's equity. There have been two lawsuits between Boxin Company, Ren Shuangcheng, and Chen Long regarding Chen Long's shareholder qualification. The continued existence of the company will inevitably cause serious damage to Chen Long's legitimate rights and interests. Moreover, because Chen Long and Ren Shuangcheng hold 49% and 51% of the shares respectively, they cannot make effective decisions on major matters in the company's management, and the mechanism of the shareholders' meeting has essentially failed, which is sufficient to prove that the company's management has encountered serious difficulties. In addition, Ren Shuangcheng, suspected of illegal and criminal acts, was placed on file for investigation by the discipline inspection and supervision department in March 2021, and there is no possibility of joint operation for the two shareholders of Boxin Company. Therefore, the statutory conditions for the dissolution of Boxin Company have been met. (3) The second-instance judgment found clear facts, applied the law correctly, and followed proper procedure. Boxin Company's claim of procedural violations lacks factual and legal basis. Furthermore, after the second-instance judgment took effect, Boxin Company failed to establish a liquidation group for liquidation within 15 days. Therefore, Chen Long has applied to the people's court for compulsory liquidation. The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province has accepted Chen Long's application and made a decision (2021) Shaanxi 01 forced liquidation No. 21-1 on July 13, 2021, entitled "Decision on Designating the Liquidation Group of Shaanxi Boxin Sports Culture Communication Co., Ltd." Currently, the liquidation group of Boxin Company is conducting liquidation matters in an orderly manner.

Upon review, this Court holds that this case is an application for retrial filed by a party, and the review should focus on whether the grounds for retrial raised by Boxin Company can be established. The corresponding focus of the review is: the probative force of the "new evidence" provided by Boxin Company; whether Chen Long has the shareholder qualification of Boxin Company and can exercise the shareholder's right to file a lawsuit for dissolution of the company; whether Boxin Company meets the statutory grounds for dissolution; and whether there are serious procedural violations in the second-instance proceedings.

Regarding the probative force of the "new evidence" provided by Boxin Company. With respect to Evidence One to Seven, upon examination, these seven pieces of evidence were already subject to court-organized cross-examination in the previous proceedings. Evidence One was adopted by the court, while Evidence Two to Seven only prove that Boxin Company had urged Chen Long to make capital contributions and attend shareholders' meetings, but are insufficient to prove that Chen Long failed to make capital contributions. Therefore, none of these seven pieces of evidence meet the formal requirements for "new evidence," nor do they have the probative force to "sufficiently overturn the original judgment or ruling." With respect to Evidence Eight, upon examination, the "Urgent Notice" was already subject to cross-examination organized by the people's court in the previous proceedings. The "Notice of Inquiry" was issued after the second-instance judgment was rendered. However, neither of the above two notices indicates or implies that Chen Long is a person participating in public administration. Moreover, an effective judgment in another case has indicated that whether Chen Long is a person participating in public administration or whether he violated relevant legal provisions has no direct connection with the legal relationship at issue in this case, and Boxin Company may seek resolution through other channels. Therefore, Evidence Eight does not have the probative force to "sufficiently overturn the original judgment or ruling." With respect to Evidence Nine, upon examination, although this criminal ruling was made after the second-instance trial, the facts found do not include the allegation raised by Boxin Company that Chen Long forced equity participation. Moreover, Chen Long only participated in the litigation as a witness. Therefore, its relevance to this case is insufficient, and it also does not have the probative force to "sufficiently overturn the original judgment or ruling." In summary, the "new evidence" submitted by Boxin Company in its application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Regarding the issue of whether Chen Long has the shareholder qualification of Boxin Company and can exercise the shareholder's right to file a lawsuit for dissolution of the company. Upon examination, the fact that Chen Long holds 49% of the shares in Boxin Company and has actually paid part of his capital contribution has been found and determined by the first-instance and second-instance judgments based on the company's articles of association, industrial and commercial registration materials, and effective judgments in other cases. Moreover, according to Article 16 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the shareholders' rights restricted due to the failure to perform or fully perform capital contribution obligations do not include the right to file a lawsuit for dissolution of the company. Boxin Company's grounds for retrial in this section are not established, and this Court does not support them.

Regarding the issue of whether Boxin Company meets the statutory grounds for dissolution. The "serious difficulties" provided in Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China include difficulties in external production and operation and difficulties in internal management. In this case, the first-instance and second-instance courts have found and determined that the mechanism of Boxin Company's shareholders' meeting has failed, the contradictions between shareholders are irreconcilable, and even after court mediation, it is still difficult to break the company deadlock. Moreover, Boxin Company's grounds for retrial also reflect that it objectively has serious difficulties in management. Therefore, the second-instance judgment's finding that Boxin Company has met the dissolution grounds provided in Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II) is not improper in terms of fact-finding and legal application. Boxin Company's grounds for retrial in this section are not established, and this Court does not support them.

Regarding the issue of whether there are serious procedural violations in the second-instance proceedings. On the one hand, Boxin Company did not specify which item of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China its alleged procedural violations correspond to, and the alleged procedural violations do not meet any specific circumstance under that article. On the other hand, on April 3, 2020, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province rendered civil judgment (2019) Shaanxi 01 Civil First Instance No. 1276 in this case, finding that there was a dispute over the capital contributions of both Chen Long and Ren Shuangcheng to Boxin Company. On April 7, 2020, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province rendered civil judgment (2020) Shaanxi 01 Civil Final No. 803 in another case, namely the dispute between Boxin Company and Chen Long over the change of shareholder registration, finding that Chen Long had performed part of his capital contribution obligations. Thereafter, the second-instance court in this case remanded the case for retrial on the ground that the facts in the original first-instance judgment were unclear. After the retrial, the first-instance court incorporated the content of civil judgment (2020) Shaanxi 01 Civil Final No. 803 into the facts found and rendered its judgment, which was upheld by the second-instance court. The above trial process complies with the statutory trial procedures. Boxin Company's grounds for retrial in this section are not established, and this Court does not support them.

In summary, Boxin Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200, items 1, 2, and 6 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

Reject the application for retrial filed by Shaanxi Boxin Sports Culture Communication Co., Ltd.
